Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Bright Cart is excited about the latency profiles. Before we proceed to signature, finance has two technical questions about how Redwood will meter and bill the workload we shared: the attached usage_sample.csv is a 48-hour dump of chat sessions.

1) We have a mix of short support messages (~200 tokens) and a small number of very long diagnostic sessions that keep a 30k token context active across multiple calls. How will those long contexts be counted? Do you charge per-call tokens or amortize across the conversation?

Hi Maya — thanks for the sample and the SOW. I pulled a short worked example below and a proposed concession for the microcall pattern you noted. High-level rules we apply:

- Metering primitives: we bill "generated + prompt" tokens per request but offer conversation-level amortization for active prefixes (prefix/KV reuse).
- Long-running context: when a conversation keeps an active KV cache (same conversation_id) we amortize the large shared prefix across calls during a 24-hour active window; subsequent rehydration after 24h counts as a new prefix.
- Rounding quantum: default unit = 64 tokens for per-call rounding. We can reduce to a 32-token quantum for pilots under 250k tokens/mo.

Worked invoice-style example (from your sample):
A) Short support call (single request, no existing prefix): user prompt 120 tok + model gen 80 tok = 200 tok -> round up to nearest 64 -> billed = 256 tokens.
B) Micro 'ping' call: prompt 2 tok + gen 1 tok = 3 tok -> round up to 64 -> billed = 64 tokens.
C) Long diagnostic session: initial call establishes prefix 30,000 tok. Over next 20 calls in 12 hours each call adds 400 tok of new prompt+gen. Billing: initial call billed full 30,400 tok (rounded to nearest 64 = 30,432). Subsequent 19 calls billed on incremental tokens only: 400 tok each -> rounded per-call to 448 each (nearest 64). BUT we apply prefix amortization credit: we subtract the prefix once across the 24h active window so effective billed tokens for the 20-call conversation = (30,400) + (19 * 400) = 37,600 tok -> after rounding per-call the invoice lines would be slightly higher due to rounding; in net we provide a prefix reuse credit that avoids charging the 30k prefix on every call.

Suggested concession for Bright Cart (pilot terms):
- Reduce rounding quantum to 32 tokens for first 3 months for usage buckets under 250k tokens/mo.
- Provide one-time microcall credit equal to 10,000 tokens applied to the first invoice to offset heartbeat inflation while you tune client-side batching.

I can convert the example into mock invoice lines if that helps. If the team prefers per-conversation rounding (aggregate then round) we can present that as an alternate (but it has different accounting implications).

--
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Sergio — quick internal note copying Markus. Good example. A couple of negotiation points we should lock before we go formal:

1) Quantum reduction: 32-token quantum for 3 months is reasonable if we gate it by a usage cap (<=250k tokens/mo) and require that they adopt client-side batching within 60 days. We need a firm clause in SOW that reverts to 64-token quantum automatically after pilot thresholds.

2) Prefix amortization: define the "active window" explicitly (24 hours is okay) and include a diagnostic clause that allows us to reclassify long-lived state as a charged artifact if they deliberately pin prefixes across accounts.

3) Microcall credit: offer a one-time 10k token credit but do not include it as an ongoing discount.

Markus — can you confirm the invoice-line wording below? If finance is OK we should add these items to the SOW and send a redline to Bright Cart.

Suggested invoice-line wording to include in SOW: "Line item X: Token metering is calculated per request; per-call tokens are rounded up to the nearest N-token quantum. For customers on pilot under 250,000 tokens/month, the quantum will be 32 tokens for a period of 90 days. Prefix/KV reuse is amortized per conversation_id over a 24-hour active window; rehydration after 24 hours is billed as a new prefix."

Kimberly
Director, Sales Ops

Maya — attaching a short mock invoice export and a 2-row comparison table for the long-session case (per-call rounding vs aggregate conversation rounding). See attachment: BrightCart_SOW_Q1.pdf (SOW redline) and usage_sample.csv (annotated).

Quick summary from the table in the attachment:
- Per-call rounding increases token count due to multiple small round-ups; in your long-diagnostic example the per-call method yields ~+2.6% token inflation relative to aggregate rounding once we include rounding per incremental call.
- Aggregate-per-conversation rounding reduces rounding noise but changes how we present line items; finance teams sometimes prefer per-call lines for traceability.
